name: Liechtenstein
summary: Uses the Swiss substance lists. Use or possession for own use is a contravention fined by the court (up to CHF 50,000); unlike Switzerland there is no 10 g cannabis rule or CHF 100 ticket.
callingForHelp: Ambulance (144) staff are bound by medical secrecy. No specific legal protection for people calling about an overdose (no Good Samaritan law).
drugChecking: No service in Liechtenstein; the nearest legal services are in Switzerland (e.g. Zurich).

bmv.title: Narcotics Ordinance with substance lists (BMV, LGBl. 2015 Nr. 132)

kjg.title: Children and Youth Act (KJG), Art. 69 on alcohol

infodrogN2O.title: Infodrog: nitrous oxide, Swiss legal situation

bvgerDxm.title: Swiss Federal Administrative Court: DXM cough medicines (category B)

lsd.note: Prohibited (list d). Own use or possession: court fine up to CHF 50,000; supply up to 3 years prison.

mushrooms.note: Hallucinogenic mushrooms (Psilocybe, Panaeolus, Conocybe, Stropharia), truffles included, are prohibited (list d).

dmt.note: Prohibited (list d), so ayahuasca is illegal. Own use: court fine up to CHF 50,000.

mescaline.note: Mescaline, peyote and San Pedro cactus are listed as prohibited (list d).

dox.note: DOM, DOB and DOC are prohibited (list d); other analogues fall under the generic phenethylamine group (list e).

nbomes.note: 25B-, 25C- and 25I-NBOMe are prohibited (list d); others fall under the generic phenethylamine group (list e).

2c-x.note: 2C-B and other common 2C-x are prohibited (list d); remaining analogues fall under the generic phenethylamine group.

2c-t-x.note: 2C-T-2 and 2C-T-7 are prohibited (list d); other 2C-T-x fall under the generic phenethylamine group.

5-meo-xxt.note: 5-MeO-DMT and 5-MeO-MiPT are named in list e (controlled like list a narcotics), which also has a generic tryptamine group.

cannabis.note: Cannabis with ≥1% THC is prohibited. No 10 g rule or on-the-spot ticket: use/possession can bring a court fine up to CHF 50,000. Low-THC (<1%) CBD legal.

ketamine.note: Controlled narcotic (list b) used as a prescription medicine; possession without prescription is an offence.

dxm.note: Not a controlled narcotic (explicitly excluded). Swiss-authorised cough medicines are category B: pharmacy or doctor supply only.

nitrous.note: Not a narcotic. No specific national rule found; Swiss chemicals rules (no supply for inhalation) may apply via the customs treaty.

amphetamines.note: Amphetamine and methamphetamine are controlled (list a): own use is court-fined, supply carries prison. ADHD drugs on prescription.

mdma.note: Prohibited (list d). Own use: fine up to CHF 50,000; supply up to 3 years, serious cases 1–20 years.

cocaine.note: Controlled narcotic. Own use: fine up to CHF 50,000; supply up to 3 years, serious cases 1–20 years.

caffeine.note: Not a controlled substance; sold freely.

alcohol.note: Alcohol from 16; spirits and alcopops from 18 (possession and use by younger people are banned).

ghb/gbl.note: GHB and GBL are controlled (list a; GBL exempt only for industrial use); 1,4-BD is in list e. Sodium oxybate on prescription.

opioids.note: Heroin is prohibited; morphine, oxycodone, fentanyl etc. are prescription-only controlled narcotics.

tramadol.note: Prescription medicine; ready-to-use products are exempt from narcotics controls (list b).

benzodiazepines.note: Controlled prescription medicines (mostly list b); designer benzodiazepines are prohibited.

maois.note: Prescription medicines. Harmala alkaloids are not listed, but ayahuasca is illegal because DMT is prohibited.
